Requirement R15 (input): Input Search Pattern. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to define a search pattern for sensor/UAV coverage..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-15.1, F-15.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-15.<F>.1, Be-15.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-15.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent (restated):** Let the pilot define a search pattern that governs how the UAV/sensor covers a geographic area — i.e., specify the coverage geometry/strategy the UAV should fly/scan.

**Function candidates:**

- **F-15.1 — Specify search-pattern geometry over a geographic area.** Goal: the pilot delimits *where* coverage happens by defining the area/track shape (e.g. lawnmower box, spiral, sector) anchored on the map. Opens a spatial-definition interaction goal.

- **F-15.2 — Parameterize a search pattern's scan attributes.** Goal: the pilot sets *how* the pattern is flown/scanned — spacing between legs, orientation/heading, speed, overlap. Opens a value-configuration goal, independent of geometry placement.

- **F-15.3 — Select a predefined search-pattern template.** Goal: the pilot picks a ready-made pattern type from a catalog and applies it, deferring detailed geometry/parameter definition. Opens a fast-selection goal for high-workload conditions.

These are genuinely distinct: F-15.1 is *spatial delimitation*, F-15.2 is *attribute tuning*, F-15.3 is *catalog selection*. In practice a full "search pattern" often needs all three, but as Functions they open different pilot goals.

My recommendation: the core of R15 is **F-15.1** — without defining the area/geometry there's no pattern to tune or apply. F-15.2 and F-15.3 are strong complements (and F-15.2 heavily reuses R11/R01 Setpoint-Panel patterns; F-15.3 reuses R05/R06 preset patterns — flag for consolidation).

Which do you want to close on, or keep more than one?

Closing both **F-15.1 — Specify search-pattern geometry over a geographic area** and **F-15.2 — Parameterize a search pattern's scan attributes** as the R15 Functions.

Moving to **Behaviour**. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. One pathway per modality per Function, plus Mixed where it earns its place.

---

**F-15.1 — Specify geometry (spatial delimitation on map):**

- **Be-15.1.1 (Touch-only):** Pilot direct-manipulates on Map — tap to drop area vertices/corners (box, sector, or polygon), drag to size/rotate the shape. Live geometry preview renders as the pilot works; commit sends. Reuses the R05/R14 map-anchored interaction surface.
- **Be-15.1.2 (Keyboard-only):** Pilot enters geometry numerically via UCP/bezel — pattern anchor coords, dimensions (length/width or radius), orientation — stepping through a small field set; map echoes each entered value. Commit via bezel OSS. This is the eyes-out / turbulence-robust path.
- **Be-15.1.3 (Mixed):** Touch to place/rough-shape the area on the map, then keyboard to refine exact dimensions/coords of the same object. Adds real value: coarse spatial placement is fast by touch, precise sizing is reliable by keyboard — but each path must still stand alone (redundancy rule).

**F-15.2 — Parameterize scan attributes (leg spacing, orientation, speed, overlap):**

- **Be-15.2.1 (Touch-only):** WAD Setpoint-style panel (re-instantiated from R11/R01) — direct keypad entry + steppers + presets for each attribute, all by touch. Commit on panel.
- **Be-15.2.2 (Keyboard-only):** Same attribute set entered via bezel rotary (step) + UCP alphanumeric (direct value), field-by-field; commit via OSS.
- **Mixed:** No distinct added value here beyond what R01/R11 already established — the Setpoint-Panel is inherently mixed-capable field-by-field, so a separate Mixed pathway would just restate the redundancy rule. Skipping it.

---

Note both F-15.2 behaviours are essentially the **shared Setpoint-Panel pattern** (R01/R11) re-instantiated with search-pattern attributes — flag for consolidation, not new design.

Recommendation: close **Be-15.1.3 (Mixed)** for F-15.1 (its coarse-touch/precise-keyboard split is the genuine multimodal win) and **Be-15.2.1/Be-15.2.2** collapsed into the reused Setpoint pattern for F-15.2.

Which behaviours do you want to close?

Closing:
- **F-15.1 → Be-15.1.3 (Mixed):** touch to place/rough-shape the area on map, keyboard to refine exact coords/dimensions; each path modality-complete standalone.
- **F-15.2 → Be-15.2.1 + Be-15.2.2:** reused Setpoint-Panel pattern — Touch (keypad/steppers/presets) and Keyboard (bezel rotary + UCP), both modality-complete.

Moving to **Structure**. 2–3 concrete element sets per closed Behaviour.

---

**F-15.1 / Be-15.1.3 — geometry definition:**

- **S-15.1.3.1 — Map-anchored geometry editor (recommended).** Extends the shared Map view (R05/R07/R14):
  - New **Search-Area overlay layer** — renders the active pattern shape (box/sector/polygon) with draggable vertex/rotate handles (Touch); live preview.
  - **Geometry Field strip** (docked to map or in the pattern detail panel) — anchor coords, length/width or radius, orientation; editable via UCP alphanumeric + bezel rotary stepping (Keyboard). Map and strip are two-way bound (touch edit updates fields, keyboard edit updates shape).
  - **Commit OSS** (bezel) + on-panel commit button (Touch).
  - Reuses: Map view, map overlay/glyph layer, commit pattern from R05/R14.

- **S-15.1.3.2 — Shape-type palette + parametric form.** A small palette (box / spiral / sector / ladder) selected first, then the same Geometry Field strip drives dimensions; map shows result but placement is form-driven, not free-drag. Less direct-manipulation, but leaner overlay. Weaker touch story — I'd hold this as fallback, not primary.

**F-15.2 / Be-15.2.1 + Be-15.2.2 — scan attributes:**

- **S-15.2.x.1 — Re-instantiated Setpoint Panel (recommended, shared).** The R01/R11 Setpoint-Panel component re-instantiated with search-pattern attribute set: leg spacing, orientation, scan speed, overlap %.
  - WAD panel: keypad direct entry + steppers + presets (Touch).
  - Bezel rotary + UCP alphanumeric (Keyboard).
  - Acknowledgment via shared R08 notification stack.
  - Flag: this is **reuse, not new** — same component family as R11.

- **S-15.2.x.2 — Inline attribute rows in the geometry panel.** Instead of a separate Setpoint Panel, fold the scan attributes as editable rows into the same F-15.1 detail panel, so geometry + attributes live in one surface. Tighter integration, single commit — but diverges from the shared Setpoint-Panel convention. Trade-off: cohesion vs. reuse consistency.

---

My recommendation: **S-15.1.3.1** (map-anchored editor) + **S-15.2.x.1** (reused Setpoint Panel), keeping F-15.1 and F-15.2 on distinct-but-adjacent surfaces bound to the same pattern object. If you'd rather one unified surface, **S-15.2.x.2** merges them at the cost of Setpoint-Panel consistency.

Which structures do you want to close?

You're right — you said "Both" meaning close **all** the behaviour candidates, not just my recommended subset. Correcting.

**Closed behaviours for R15:**

**F-15.1 — Specify geometry:**
- **Be-15.1.1 (Touch-only):** tap vertices / drag-size-rotate shape on Map, live preview, commit.
- **Be-15.1.2 (Keyboard-only):** enter anchor coords, dimensions, orientation via UCP/bezel, map echoes, commit OSS.
- **Be-15.1.3 (Mixed):** touch to place/rough-shape, keyboard to refine exact values.

**F-15.2 — Parameterize scan attributes:**
- **Be-15.2.1 (Touch-only):** Setpoint-style panel — keypad entry + steppers + presets, all touch.
- **Be-15.2.2 (Keyboard-only):** same attributes via bezel rotary + UCP, field-by-field, OSS commit.
- **Be-15.2.3 (Mixed):** field-by-field mix on the Setpoint Panel (touch some fields, keyboard others).

(Note: I'd earlier argued Be-15.2.3 Mixed adds no distinct value — it's just the inherent mixed-capability of the shared Setpoint Panel. Logging it as closed per your call, but flagging it's not a separate design effort, it falls out of the same structure.)

---

Now **Structure**. Since all six behaviours are closed, the structures must cover all pathways — but the earlier proposal already does, because the touch/keyboard/mixed pathways are all served by the same bound surfaces:

**F-15.1 (Be-15.1.1 / .1.2 / .1.3):**
- **S-15.1.x.1 — Map-anchored geometry editor (recommended):** Search-Area overlay layer with draggable handles (serves Touch Be-15.1.1) + two-way-bound Geometry Field strip via UCP/bezel (serves Keyboard Be-15.1.2); binding between them serves Mixed Be-15.1.3. Commit via OSS + on-panel button. Reuses Map view + overlay/commit pattern (R05/R14).
- **S-15.1.x.2 — Shape-type palette + parametric form:** palette selects shape, field strip drives dimensions; weaker direct-manipulation touch story. Fallback.

**F-15.2 (Be-15.2.1 / .2.2 / .2.3):**
- **S-15.2.x.1 — Re-instantiated Setpoint Panel (recommended, shared reuse from R01/R11):** keypad/steppers/presets (Touch), bezel rotary + UCP (Keyboard), any field-by-field mix (Mixed). Ack via shared R08 stack.
- **S-15.2.x.2 — Inline attribute rows folded into the F-15.1 geometry panel:** unified surface, single commit; diverges from Setpoint-Panel convention.

Recommendation stands: **S-15.1.x.1 + S-15.2.x.1**.

Which structures do you want to close?
